Endelevu OÜ is an Estonian research and technology company developing satellite-based Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) solutions for afforestation and reforestation carbon projects in sub-Saharan Africa.
The company processes ESA Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellite data through a proprietary algorithm stack built specifically for East African ecological conditions — addressing the persistent cloud cover, bi-modal growing seasons, and smallholder parcel scales that make standard global monitoring tools unreliable in the region. The intended output is audit-ready compliance documentation aligned with Verra's VM0047 ARR carbon methodology, enabling project developers and landowners to meet regulatory verification requirements through satellite-derived data rather than costly field surveys.
Endelevu's pipeline integrates cloud-penetrating SAR monitoring, multispectral optical analysis, and AI-based land cover classification into a single automated workflow — from raw satellite data to formatted compliance document. The service targets individual project developers, carbon aggregators, and Verra-accredited Verification and Validation Bodies operating across Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, and Tanzania, with planned expansion to wider sub-Saharan Africa and South America.
The founding team combines first-hand operational experience in East Africa, satellite Earth Observation engineering, and research-grade machine learning expertise. Endelevu OÜ was incorporated in October 2025 and is registered in the Estonian Business Register under number 17343299.

entityDescription:
The Thünen Institute of Forest Ecosystems is a federal research body under the German Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture. Located in Eberswalde, it conducts ecological research to develop sustainable strategies for forest management, climate protection, and nature conservation. The institute's activities are divided into four main areas:
Forest Resources & Climate Protection: Uses remote sensing and the National Forest Inventory to model forest development and report on forests' contribution to carbon storage and renewable resources.
Soil Protection & Forest Health: Monitors forest soils and vitality to understand risks, particularly how changing environments and pollution affect tree health.
Forest Ecology & Biodiversity: Measures material and energy flows to analyze the resilience and adaptability of forest ecosystems.
Wildlife Ecology: Studies the intersection and balance between forest management and game / wildlife populations.
Additionally, the institute houses the International Cooperative Programme (ICP Forests) Programme Coordinating Centre to monitor forest conditions across Europe.

entityDescription:
The Institute for European Energy and Climate Policy (IEECP) is a non-for-profit, independent research organisation. We act as a knowledge-hub sharing pragmatic results as well as innovative ideas providing policymakers, and all private and public decision-makers, independent expertise and science-based research to support their work towards the energy transition and a sustainable future.
Founded in 2015, IEECP’s international interdisciplinary team of experts has grown progressively to reach 36 persons by 2024, working on science-based climate change mitigation, energy efficiency and renewable energy policy, generating and disseminating scientific knowledge, and proposing data-driven solutions, hands-on solutions and policy recommendations as well as strategic communication.
IEECP has a rich experience in managing EU, climate action and energy transition projects, primarily within EU-funded programmes (previously Horizon 2020 and now LIFE and Horizon Europe). Since 2015, IEECP has been coordinator of 25 EU-funded projects, and partner of further 41 projects.
Most of the projects are related to the energy efficiency field: cross-cutting energy efficiency policies (e.g. EEOS – Energy Efficiency Obligation Schemes), energy efficiency financing and energy efficiency in companies, energy performance of buildings, behavioural changes. Part of these projects have a focus on tackling energy poverty and supporting vulnerable households. All these projects are strongly related to the implementation of the EU Directives in the field, especially the EED and EPBD, and support experience sharing among Member States to improve national policies. Another part of our projects deal with local action for climate and energy, for integrated approaches addressing climate mitigation and adaptation.
Our roles in these projects included policy review and benchmarking, data analysis, preparing policy briefs and recommendations, developing tools and libraries of resources, leading capacity building and training programmes. In addition, we have been leading the Work Packages for stakeholder engagement, and for communication and dissemination in many of these projects.
The IEECP team is multidisciplinary, with backgrounds in policy analysis, economics, engineering, and social and communication sciences. While being a Dutch-based foundation, IEECP experts are based all over Europe, in Belgium, Croatia, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Portugal, the Netherlands and the UK. The team is highly multicultural, speaking more than 20 languages, and pays particular attention to gender equality, diversity and inclusivity, both in the organisation and in its work.
IEECP experts are also actively involved in the expert and scientific communities. For example, Vlasis Oikonomou and Jean-Sébastien Broc were guest editors of a special issue on Energy Efficiency First of theEnergy Efficiencyjournal (Springer ed.) and are reviewers for several scientific journals of Elsevier (Energy,Energy Policy,Energy Economics,Smart Energy,Energy Research & Social Science,Journal of Cleaner Production) and Springer (Energy Efficiency,Journal of Government and Policy,Mitigation and Adaptation Strategies for Global Change). They also have been panel leaders for the ECEEE (European Council for an Energy Efficient Economy) Summer Study. Jean-Sébastien is also a board member of the Energy Evaluation association (formerly IEPPEC), and has been co-chair of the IEPPEC conference in 2014 and 2016. Ivana Rogulj has been member of the Steering Committee of the Covenant of Companies for Climate and Energy, and of EEFIG (Energy Efficiency Financial Institutions Group). Giulia Pizzini is board member of ECEEE (European Council for an Energy Efficient Economy).

EPAK GmbH is a German engineering and development company specializing in advanced communication, radar, and sensor technologies. With more than 25 years of experience, the company covers the full innovation chain from fundamental research and system design to prototyping, manufacturing, and operational validation. EPAK’s activities span satellite communications for maritime and land-mobile “on-the-move” scenarios, high-frequency and radar engineering, optical communications, robotics, and multi-sensor systems.
EPAK contributes to national and European research programs and serves as an established industrial partner for scientific institutions and high-technology industries. Technologies developed by EPAK are utilized, among others, in the SABBIA project of the Fraunhofer Institute for High Frequency Physics and Radar Techniques (FHR), enabling object localization through the analysis of DVB-S2 signal waveforms from geostationary satellites. A long-standing collaboration with the Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits (IIS) includes system-level testing of automatically steered antenna systems in the FORTE measurement chamber in Ilmenau. These tests address dynamic motion profiles, objective performance evaluation, and methodological improvements for mobile antenna systems.
EPAK has established a broad portfolio of satellite-communication technologies deployed worldwide and maintains long-term partnerships with industrial stakeholders. In cooperation with AIRBUS, the company supplies maritime SATCOM systems for the German Armed Forces. EPAK has also participated in several development programs with the German Aerospace Center (DLR), including UniLandKom-Pro (FKZ 50RK1927), UniLandKom (FKZ 50YB1604), PROSAT-Pro (FKZ 50YB1413) and PROSAT (FKZ 50YB1318).
Building on extensive experience with mechanically stabilized VSAT terminals for GEO and LEO satellites, EPAK has expanded its research focus toward electronically steerable antenna systems. The proliferation of large LEO constellations (e.g., SpaceX, OneWeb) has accelerated work on phased-array architectures, which now represent a central component of the company’s technological roadmap. Current research includes high-frequency front-end modules, beamforming and calibration algorithms, multi-sensor fusion for stabilization and tracking, and low-latency control concepts for mobile platforms.
EPAK maintains comprehensive in-house capabilities in power electronics, digital and analog circuit design, RF engineering, antenna and feed-system development, sensor-integration, and control-algorithm engineering. CAD-based mechanical design and strong links to regional manufacturing partners enable rapid realization of prototypes and small-series demonstrators. This integrated capability supports efficient translation of research results into validated system prototypes and technology demonstrators.

The company applies state of the art mathematical techniques, for the creation, implementation, and interpretation of validated predictive models for big data analysis, personalised medicine, clinical trials, computer aided drug discovery, risk assessment and materials science.
